newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ministers approve 30,000 tonnes U.S. malt barley quota.
newsitem.headline: Ministers approve 30,000 tonnes U.S. malt barley quota.

text.p: Farm ministers approved on Tuesday the opening of a 30,000-tonne tariff quota for imports of U.S. malting barley on condition that Washington withdraw its complaint to the World Trade Organisation, an EU official said.
The U.S. was due to request on Thursday the opening of a WTO trade disputes panel to investigate the complaint which also includes EU cereals import duties.
It had complained about the delay in opening the quota which will compensate exporters for the loss of Austrian, Swedish and Finnish markets after these countries joined the EU in 1995,
The EU official added that Italy, Spain and Portugal voted against opening the import quota allowing imports at 50 percent of the normal tariff. It is due to take effect on May 5.
A European Commission spokesman added that the EU's executive would shortly adopt a new cumulative rice import tariff system in response to U.S. complaints.
The cumulative recovery system allows traders to claim back any overpaid duties.
"Importers will have to decide whether they are in or out of the system," the spokesman said, adding they couldn't choose on a shipment by shipment basis.
The EU decided that the original import tariff system based on invoices was open to fraud and proposed a system based on market reference prices.
But the U.S. complained that the reference price system, which also applies to cereal imports, infringed WTO rules.
